en: Typhoon Haiyan, known locally as Yolanda, struck the Philippines in 2013 as one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded at landfall.
The famous Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of cone-shaped limestone mounds formed from ancient marine fossils.
The Agusan River flows northward into Butuan Bay, draining rainwater from the Caraga region back into the Bohol Sea.
NASA's Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater on Mars to search for ancient microbial life in a dried-up river delta.
Sirius, also known as the Dog Star, is the brightest star visible in the night sky from Earth.
The Apollo 11 astronauts landed in the Sea of Tranquility, a large, dark basaltic plain on the Moon.
Mount Pinatubo's massive 1991 eruption injected millions of tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, temporarily cooling global temperatures.
The fertile volcanic soil surrounding Mount Mayon in Albay is rich in minerals that help local farmers grow abundant abaca plants.
Baguio City experiences a subtropical highland climate, making it significantly cooler than the lowland areas of the Philippines year-round.
The Amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
The Lepanto copper mine in Mankayan, Benguet, produces valuable copper minerals that are essential for making electrical wires.
Jupiter's moon Europa has a smooth, icy surface that scientists believe hides a massive, liquid water ocean underneath.
